title: Reciprocal sums over infinite exponent supports
question: Is the sum of 1/(2^n-1) over every infinite set of positive exponents irrational?
authority_posture: not_registered; the claim registry does not carry these declarations and kernel checking them does not promote them into reviewed public claims
what_is_checked: That the strict Mersenne tail inequality is hereditary under deleting an arbitrary collection of future weights.
That binary digit strings restricted to any chosen support retain unique Mersenne coding.
Restricted sets are compact and nowhere dense; infinite-support sets are perfect; finite-complement measure is 2^(-|F|), otherwise zero.
what_is_not_checked: The universal irrationality problem, or irrationality for any new infinite support.
Fair-bit laws, finer singularity results, and periodic-stride dimensions.
Any bridge from geometric uniqueness or measure rigidity to arithmetic irrationality.

open_obligations.statement: Convert hereditary unique coding into an arithmetic obstruction to rational values for every infinite support, including zero-measure Cantor supports.
Extend the measure dichotomy to Bernoulli laws and periodic-stride dimensions without implying arithmetic consequences.

main_results.contribution_class: mixed prior-art geometry and locally proved metric result; novelty unassessed
main_results.statement: The base-2 Mersenne achievement set has Lebesgue measure exactly one.
main_results.boundary: This does not decide whether every infinite-support sum is irrational.

main_results.statement: For every integer base b >= 2, the full-support Erdos-Borwein series is irrational.
main_results.boundary: This is the classical full-support theorem, not universal Erdos #257.

main_results.statement: For every integer base b >= 2 and every infinite pairwise-coprime support A with summable reciprocal mass, the support-restricted Mersenne series is irrational.
main_results.boundary: This is the pairwise-coprime support theorem, not universal Erdos #257; the infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses remain explicit.

main_results.statement: For every integer base b >= 2 and every eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence γ with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region, the series sum_a γ(a)/(b^a - 1) is irrational.
main_results.boundary: This is the nonnegative rational eventually-periodic coefficient theorem; its nonnegativity, eventual periodicity, and positive-tail hypotheses remain explicit, and the broader mixed-sign periodic theorem is not claimed.

main_results.statement: For every support A carrying the finite-core OrthogonalPetalBouquet structure and satisfying the exact uniform SunflowerForcedSlotTailSelection predicate, the base-2 support-restricted Mersenne series erdosSupportSeries 2 A is irrational.
main_results.boundary: This is a conditional reduction: the bouquet structure and uniform tail-selection predicate remain hypotheses; neither is constructed for arbitrary supports, so this does not add an unconditional Erdos #257 support family or solve the universal problem.

main_results.statement: For a reduced finite Mersenne sum, the base order modulo the denominator equals the support lcm.
main_results.boundary: The finite-support theorem does not settle any infinite-support sum.

main_results.statement: A support-restricted Mersenne achievement set has exact finite-complement measure or measure zero for infinite complement.
main_results.boundary: The measure dichotomy does not classify rational points.

main_results.statement: A rational support value with a positive support seed and denominator 2^c*v produces a positive natural shifted tail state with an exact binary recurrence and a modular doubling orbit modulo v.
main_results.boundary: This state-extraction theorem does not exclude rational infinite supports or settle universal Erdős #257; the support and rational-value hypotheses remain explicit.

main_results.contribution_class: locally proved exact equivalence plus conditional consequences; novelty unassessed
main_results.statement: For p : ℤ and q > 0, a nonempty positive-index support with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = p/q exists exactly when a quotient-only Boolean–Möbius carry certificate exists, with positive square-root-bounded integer orbit, divisible carry differences, and support reconstructed from its Boolean Möbius transform.
main_results.boundary: The equivalence is stated at the existence level with q > 0, 0 ∉ A, and a positive support witness; it gives no contradiction, no universal Erdős #257 irrationality result, and no producer of cofinally nonintegral shifts for the actual recurrence. The generic tempered-orbit theorem and the reciprocal-mass, unbounded-tail, and zero-window results are subordinate consequences, not separate families; the zero-window constant depends on the support and numerator and is not uniform. This does not settle every infinite support, and no novelty, priority, significance, external-review, or unrestricted #257 endpoint claim is made.

main_results.statement: If positive rational-greedy skips occur cofinally in the declared sense, the skipped-core construction supplies cofinally many exact local Mersenne half rows and hence (1 / 2 : ℝ) belongs to the Mersenne achievement set.
main_results.boundary: This route is conditional on the unproved CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips premise: for every N there is c ≥ max N 4 with a positive greedy remainder below mersenneWeightRat c. A finite exact row or any finite collection of exact rows does not establish that cofinal supply. The result is a conditional 1/2-membership/counterexample route only, not an unconditional solution of Erdős #257; the exact-row, upper-half Boolean-word, rank-two, and endpoint-defect declarations are subordinate mechanism evidence, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

main_results.contribution_class: locally proved exact endpoint classification; novelty unassessed
main_results.statement: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to unbounded false successor terminal bits, equivalently to an unbounded upper-or-middle successor branch, cofinal terminal-false positions, unbounded skipped ranks along the integer seam, infinite greedy skipped support, and no last half-greedy skip.
main_results.boundary: This exact endpoint-socket classification does not supply any unbounded terminal-false or upper-or-middle occurrences, cofinal supply, skipped-support producer, or half-membership witness; finite exact rows do not establish the required global supply. It is not an unconditional or universal Erdős #257 result, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

main_results.statement: For a positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a*x splits into the coefficient at x, the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, and an exact finite composite-dilation defect.
main_results.boundary: The exact defect is not bounded for arbitrary supports and supplies no tail selector or irrationality theorem; the separate bouquet budget remains conditional on its structural hypotheses.

main_results.statement: For positive odd integers p, D, and q, the integer form of the two-thirds band forces p ≥ 7; the small odd numerator classes 1, 3, and 5 are therefore excluded.
main_results.boundary: This is local 2-adic band arithmetic: p = 7 is sharp for the stated hypotheses, and the theorem does not prove that an actual half-greedy orbit reaches or avoids the band, nor does it prove half-membership.

families.summary: The multiplicative order of the base modulo a reduced finite-sum denominator is the support lcm, forcing denominator growth.
families.boundary: A finite-support denominator theorem does not settle an infinite-support sum.

families.contribution_class: locally proved exact equivalence plus conditional consequences; novelty unassessed
families.summary: For p : ℤ and q > 0, a nonempty normalized positive-index support with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = p/q exists exactly when a quotient-only Boolean–Möbius carry certificate U exists. The certificate has U 0 = p, positive U, the square-root bound U(N) ≤ q(2√N + 4), q-divisible carry differences, and a Boolean Möbius transform; the converse reconstructs the support from that transform. This quotient-level equivalence is distinct from the shifted natural-tail state family.
families.boundary: The equivalence is stated at the existence level with q > 0, 0 ∉ A, and a positive support witness; it gives no contradiction, no universal Erdős #257 irrationality result, and no producer of cofinally nonintegral shifts for the actual recurrence. The generic tempered-orbit theorem and the reciprocal-mass, unbounded-tail, and zero-window results are subordinate consequences, not separate families; the zero-window constant depends on the support and numerator and is not uniform. This does not settle every infinite support, and no novelty, priority, significance, external-review, or unrestricted #257 endpoint claim is made.

families.summary: If CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips holds—cofinally many positive rational-greedy remainders below the next Mersenne weight—the skipped-core and upper-half Boolean-word construction supplies cofinally many exact local half rows, yielding (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet. The load-bearing representative is half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips; exact-row construction, endpoint-defect transition, forced rank-two membership, and Boolean-word filling are subordinate mechanisms.
families.boundary: CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips is an unproved global supply premise: for every N there must be c ≥ max N 4 with a positive greedy remainder below mersenneWeightRat c. Finite exact rows, including one produced by a skipped core, do not establish cofinality. This is a conditional 1/2-membership/counterexample route, not an unconditional Erdős #257 solution; the rank-two, endpoint-defect, and upper-half Boolean-word declarations remain subordinate evidence, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

families.contribution_class: locally proved exact endpoint classification; novelty unassessed
families.summary: Membership of 1/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is exactly equivalent to unbounded false successor terminal bits, the unbounded upper-or-middle seam branch, cofinal terminal-false positions, unbounded skipped ranks along the integer seam, infinite greedy skipped support, and the absence of a last half-greedy skip. The load-bearing representative is half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_unboundedTerminalFalse; the remaining equivalences are subordinate endpoint-socket evidence.
families.boundary: This exact endpoint-socket classification does not supply any unbounded terminal-false or upper-or-middle occurrences, cofinal supply, skipped-support producer, or half-membership witness; finite exact rows do not establish the required global supply. It is not an unconditional or universal Erdős #257 result, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

families.summary: A rational support fraction produces a positive natural shifted tail state satisfying the exact binary recurrence and modular doubling orbit modulo v.
families.boundary: The state-extraction theorem does not exclude rational infinite supports or settle universal Erdős #257; the support and rational-value hypotheses remain explicit.

families.summary: The composite support-dilation identity splits the new divisor count into the old coefficient, the distinguished divisor, and an exact finite defect; its bouquet specialization supplies a separate structural budget.
families.boundary: The exact defect is not bounded for arbitrary supports and supplies no tail selector or irrationality theorem; the bouquet budget remains conditional on its structural hypotheses.

families.summary: Full, factorial, power-of-two, multiple, eventually periodic, residue-class, and odd supports are formalised; pairwise-coprime support is split out as a dedicated non-dilation representative.
families.evidence_mode: Lean kernel plus Comparator for full and pairwise-coprime support
families.boundary: Structured known families do not cover arbitrary infinite supports.

families.summary: Infinite pairwise-coprime supports with summable reciprocal mass have irrational Mersenne support series by an adaptive CRT and weighted coefficient certificate argument.
families.boundary: This structured support theorem does not settle arbitrary infinite supports; its infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses remain explicit.

families.summary: An eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence with a positive value in its periodic region has an irrational Lambert–Mersenne series; denominator clearing reduces the rational sequence to a periodic Nat-weight certificate.
families.boundary: This does not claim the broader mixed-sign periodic theorem; all coefficient, positivity, base, period, and threshold hypotheses remain explicit.

families.summary: A finite-core orthogonal-petal bouquet together with the exact uniform tail-selection predicate composes through the forced-carry certificate consumer to irrationality; the explicit alternating-core, squared-prime-petal witness shows the structural class is non-vacuous, but the selector remains open.
families.evidence_mode: Lean kernel plus Comparator plus paper argument
families.boundary: The bouquet and selector hypotheses remain explicit; the selector is not proved, so this is not an unconditional #257 support family.

families.contribution_class: Lean structure plus paper and external theorem
families.summary: Lean checks squarefree incidence and no-go statements; the irrationality conclusion uses an external analytic theorem in the paper.
families.evidence_mode: Lean kernel plus paper argument plus cited theorem
families.boundary: Comparator must not badge the paper-plus-external conclusion.

families.contribution_class: mixed prior-art geometry and locally proved metric result; novelty unassessed
families.summary: Compactness, perfectness, total disconnectedness, nowhere density, and measure one for the unrestricted achievement set.
families.boundary: Geometry of the full set does not decide irrationality of every coded point.

families.summary: Support-restricted coding is injective and the associated achievement set has exact finite-complement measure or zero for infinite complement.
families.boundary: The measure dichotomy does not classify rational points.

families.summary: Exact greedy characterisations, finite-support exclusions, the odd 2-adic two-thirds-band bound, and two conditional rational-half countermodel frontiers isolate local constraints around the remaining 1/2 and 1/21 alternatives.
families.boundary: Neither membership question is decided; the 2-adic bound is sharp locally, and the two countermodel routes require unconstructed terminal-scaled or cofinal-cylinder antecedents.

paper.title: Weighted Support Criteria for Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
paper.subject: Erdős #257
paper.question: Which Mersenne-support subseries are settled, what finite-period and achievement-set structure is proved, and what still blocks Erdős #257?
paper.precis: Fix a finite nonempty prime set P and put h(a)=∏_{p∈P}p^{v_p(a)}. If an infinite support A has ∑_{a∈A}h(a)/(a(2^{h(a)}−1)) finite, its reciprocal Mersenne subseries is irrational at every integer base b≥2, as is the subseries on every infinite subset of A. The paper prints a complete ordinary proof and a host with divergent reciprocal sum, so the criterion is strictly weaker than reciprocal summability. A common observation window also proves hereditary irrationality for unions of weighted supports and strengthened positive-cover supports. These are ordinary results, not Lean theorems, and no priority claim is made. Universal Erdős #257 remains open.
paper.owns: problem-specific mathematical exposition for Erdős #257: exact finite-prime weighted support criterion, mixed weighted-and-cover support theorem and their ordinary proofs, exact finite periods, settled support families, method limits, and the open half-value edge
paper.not_authority_for: the validity of claims tagged Lean, which belongs to the cited kernel-checked source, or a solution to Erdős #257, which remains open

papers.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
papers.subject: Erdős #257
papers.question: What has been tried on Erdős #257, which routes are closed, and what exact universal and half-value obligations remain?
papers.precis: The record prints the complete ordinary proof of the finite-prime weighted support criterion, including all-base hereditary irrationality and a reciprocal-divergent host, and the common-witness proof for mixed weighted-and-cover supports. These proofs are not formalised in Lean. It also retains finite-denominator noncollapse; exact restricted-set coding, topology, perfectness, and measure; a squarefree-support method boundary; and an exact carry-pivot normal form. Prime support at base 2 and squarefree support at power-of-two bases are identified as cited prior results. The targets 1/2 and 1/21 have no finite-support representation and reduce to explicit infinite-orbit alternatives. Neither target membership nor universal #257 is decided.
papers.owns: a claim-bounded problem-specific reasoning surface for Erdős #257: selected checked premises, finite computations, closed routes, surviving obligations, and their exact evidence bands
papers.not_authority_for: the validity of claims tagged Lean, which belongs to the cited kernel-checked source, or a solution to Erdős #257, whose universal and half-value questions remain open
